scope: Bounded review of all nine Australian electoral commission hubs and targeted official election, vacancy and replacement sources. This is not an exhaustive council, parliamentary vacancy, candidate, result, political-party or current-officeholder audit.
method: Independent concurrent reviews distinguished ordinary native-origin responses from readable official web-source copies and unsuccessful requests. Six scoped content releases require their actual separate publication receipts. Unchanged canonical facts, candidate observations and inaccessible underlying records retain their earlier evidence and dates.

commissions.outcome: No material election or vacancy change verified.
findings: The reviewed home, 2026 media and by-election indexes returned ordinary native HTTP 200. Farrer on 9 May remains the latest listed by-election.

The dated 26 November disclosure statement described legislation awaiting Royal Assent at that publication time. The 27 November signage action is an administrative electoral-law item, not a newly announced election or vacancy.
limits: The dated disclosure statement is not a fresh determination of the legislation's present assent or commencement status.
This is not a complete Commonwealth parliamentary vacancy, membership or political-party register audit.
commissions.reportSummary: Native election and media hubs were readable. Farrer remains the latest listed by-election; dated disclosure and signage statements establish no new election. Present legal commencement, every parliamentary vacancy and all members were not audited.

commissions.outcome: Three missing detailed timetables verified; separate releases for Kempsey, Walcha and Tenterfield A Ward.
findings: Ordinary native HTTP 200 event pages, updated 25 or 26 November, publish detailed timetables for the retained 16 January 2027 Kempsey, Walcha and Tenterfield A Ward by-elections. Their notices and timetable rows distinguish residential enrolment, nominations, postal applications, dispatch, early voting, polling, receipt and scheduled declaration.

The 23 November enrolment milestones are historical timetable entries, not new dates to be inferred from the review clock. Coffs Harbour and Hunters Hill South retain five and four ballot entries respectively; Cobar remains uncontested.
limits: Published clock times are recorded literally without an inferred timezone or offset-bearing countdown; opening clock times absent from a row remain absent.
Accepted nominations, results, member profiles and all council notices were not exhaustively re-reconciled. Kempsey's non-residential-roll evidence remains distinct from the general residential roll.
commissions.reportSummary: Native sources supplied three detailed January by-election timetables, published as separate Kempsey, Walcha and Tenterfield A Ward changes. Literal times carry no newly inferred timezone. Coffs Harbour/Hunters Hill South ballots and Cobar's uncontested status match; full candidate and roster coverage is not claimed.

commissions.outcome: State-election counting phase verified; no winner or current-office change inferred.
findings: The election hub's current official web-source text says counting has begun. Separate Assembly and Council progressive-results routes returned ordinary native HTTP 200 during the independent review at approximately 07:37 UTC.

The state-election guide and its 96 canonical place dependants receive the same counting phase, with no transient vote totals. Earlier 495 announcement/preselection records remain separate from the 13 November 1,037 official ballot-entry snapshot.
Knox Baird Ward's electoral roll closed on 25 November under its existing timetable; its other future milestones match earlier evidence.
limits: Progressive figures are provisional. No declared winner, new government, serving-member replacement, individual ballot refresh or complete Parliament/council audit is claimed.
Native hub access and readable official web bodies are distinguished in the scoped counting evidence.
commissions.reportSummary: The VEC confirms counting and separate provisional chamber results. Native result routes were readable; no totals or winners were imported. Knox Baird Ward's roll closure matches its retained timetable. Candidate, officeholder and earlier-result dates remain separate.

commissions.outcome: No material election or vacancy change verified.
findings: Official web-source copies crawled today retain Redland's 12 December full postal by-election and the latest 19 November notice naming twelve candidates in ballot order. Postal completion remains 12 December at 6 pm and receipt 22 December at 5 pm.
Tablelands Division 1 remains a past event. The older Brisbane boundary-consultation notice establishes neither a determined map edition nor a new poll.
limits: Initial ordinary native requests had a DNS failure; retries of the election, Redland and media pages returned HTTP 403. Official retrieved copies are not represented as fresh origin responses.

Dedicated Redland nomination monitoring ended 19 November. It was not restarted; current candidate-grid observations and D’Rose history retain their earlier dates. No exhaustive Queensland council, party, roster or result audit is claimed.
commissions.reportSummary: Native requests failed, then returned 403; official copies crawled today retain Redland's twelve-candidate full postal event and separate completion/receipt deadlines. Dedicated nomination monitoring was not restarted, and candidate observation dates remain unchanged.

commissions.outcome: Gingin Council decision verified; commission December timetable unchanged.
findings: Reviewed WAEC hubs, December event details and notice 2642 returned ordinary native HTTP 200 between approximately 07:36 and 07:38 UTC. The December postal-vote receipt deadline remains 3 December at 6 pm. The 26 November roll-scan item is administrative information, not an election result.

Gingin's published 17 November meeting minutes, item 11.1 on pages 14-16, record the unanimous 7/0 decision to leave Jason Weeks's vacancy unfilled until the 2027 ordinary election, noting Electoral Commissioner approval. No exact future polling date is established.
Bridgetown-Greenbushes' current notices/news and 5 November minutes were natively readable and retain 18 March 2027 for its extraordinary postal election.
limits: Gingin minutes' introductory confirmation date is blank, so no later confirmation date is inferred. PDF text was available; web screenshot returned cache miss.
Carnarvon, Coolgardie and Esperance current election pages were natively readable, but all ballots, withdrawals and rosters were not exhaustively audited. No security bypass was attempted.
commissions.reportSummary: Native WAEC pages retain 3 December postal receipt at 6 pm. Published Gingin minutes resolve its pending decision: leave the vacancy until the 2027 ordinary election, with no exact poll day. Bridgetown's 18 March postal event matches; full candidate/withdrawal/roster coverage remains partial.

commissions.outcome: No material election or timetable change verified.
findings: Five ECSA hubs and the 8 July timetable notice returned ordinary native HTTP 200. Previously recorded January enrolment/nomination, February nomination-close, March mail-out and April voting-close milestones match. No new specific supplementary election was verified.
limits: The Council Elections key-dates portal returned native HTTP 403 and the web reader timed out twice. Its failed requests are not no-change evidence.
Near-request ECSA Last-Modified values are not treated as publication dates. Council exceptions, all nominees, current rosters and individual results remain outside this bounded review.
commissions.reportSummary: Five native ECSA hubs and the dated timetable notice match earlier milestones. The separate key-dates portal returned 403 and web timeouts. No source-date bump, newly inferred timezone or exhaustive council/roster assurance is claimed.

commissions.outcome: Known pending vacancy and Legislative Council period unchanged.
findings: Native requests to the three hubs returned HTTP 403 under ordinary TLS. Official home and Legislative Council web copies were crawled today; the vacancies copy was crawled yesterday.

Derwent Valley retains Michelle Dracoulis' 16 November resignation and the candidate-consent deadline of noon on 30 November, with result pending. Legislative Council material gives May 2027 for Derwent, Mersey and Windermere without an exact polling day.
limits: Retrieved-copy freshness is not a fresh native-origin response. Candidate consents, recount time, declared result and full rosters were not freshly established.
Existing Hobart timing and other unchanged canonical evidence retain their separate dates. No security weakening or bypass was attempted.
commissions.reportSummary: Native requests returned 403. Today's home/Legislative Council copies and yesterday's vacancy copy retain Derwent Valley's noon 30 November consent deadline and pending outcome, plus May 2027 Council elections without an exact day. No result or full roster reconciliation is claimed.

commissions.outcome: No material election, vacancy or determined-boundary change verified.
findings: Ordinary native HTTP 200 reads of home, elections, the 11th Assembly vacancy register and redistribution detail retain the existing election date and Rattenbury/Vassarotti vacancy outcome. The register still records one casual vacancy since the 2024 election.
Public redistribution suggestions/comments have closed. The proposal is anticipated in early 2027; proposal and final determination remain pending rather than a new serving boundary edition.
limits: The web reader timed out on the vacancy register, but a fresh ordinary native response supplied its body. Other ACT official web copies and native bodies were distinguished.
No complete Assembly membership or political-party register audit, new member, legal change or new boundary edition is claimed.
commissions.reportSummary: Fresh native home, election, vacancy-register and redistribution bodies match the existing election and casual-vacancy records. Redistribution consultation is closed and the proposal/final determination remain pending; no new map or full Assembly/party audit is inferred.

commissions.outcome: Milngin early-voting close corrected; summary opening conflict explicit.
findings: Two detailed official HTML sources, read as retrieved web copies, give Darwin early voting from 30 November to 2 December, 8:30 am to 4 pm. Both canonical events correct the 2 December close from 6 pm to 4 pm. The currently linked detailed programme text independently agrees.

The summary timetable updated 23 November instead prints early voting from 23 November at 8:30 am. The 30 November opening is retained from the detailed sources with that discrepancy explicit. Mobile voting remains separately scheduled from 23 November at 9 am.

The current candidate list and declaration retain two candidates for one vacancy and the MCTAGGART/McTahhart spelling discrepancy. Candidate check dates remain 21 November. Postal application, dispatch, completion and receipt evidence remain separate from counting.
limits: Ordinary native requests to the NTEC hubs, candidate/timetable/voting detail and final PDF returned HTTP 403. The web home and summary were crawled today; current-election copy two days ago; candidate list six days ago; voting options five days ago; dated 20 November release six days ago; notice copies older.
The detailed PDF text was crawled three days ago and marked correct as at 20 November; its screenshot returned cache miss. The changed close relies independently on both HTML sources.
Existing Australia/Darwin offsets retain earlier reviewed timezone evidence; no newly printed ACST wording, polling-close inference from the counting row, winner or current office is asserted.
commissions.reportSummary: Native requests returned 403. Two detailed official HTML copies establish the 4 pm early-voting close; the summary's conflicting opening date is retained explicitly. Candidate dates, earlier timezone evidence and separate postal/polling milestones remain intact. PDF visual verification was unavailable.

Published 17 November minutes record the decision to leave the vacancy until the 2027 ordinary election. No exact future day, candidate or replacement member inferred.

reviewLimits: This bounded review does not certify every council or parliamentary vacancy notice, candidate, withdrawal, profile, party register, historical contest or current officeholder.

Access failures preserve the last verified record and remain unresolved access limits. They are not evidence of no change. Native origin responses and retrieved official web copies have different freshness.
Elapsed dates do not declare winners, replace serving members, generate new cycles or convert counting milestones into polling-close evidence.
Unchanged canonical observations keep their earlier dates. A report dated 28 November is not a claim that every linked historical record was freshly reviewed.
No cloud browser was available. Publication and live HTTP verification do not establish responsive layout, interaction or accessibility acceptance.
